title: Tech Note: Using a generic method to create cross tab reports
author: Gary Brocks, Software Evangelist, 4D, Inc.
featured_technology: Cross-tab report generation via QR SET REPORT KIND(qr cross report)
Formulas and methods as report data sources (pointers to fields/methods)
QR SET INFO COLUMN / QR SET TOTALS DATA with pointer parameters

historical_commentary.text: Gary Brocks builds a single generic, heavily parameterized method, Rpt_QRCrsTabReports, that can generate seven different cross-tab reports for a fictitious video-rental invoicing database by passing in pointers to data-source fields, a custom quarter-labeling method as a data source, format strings, titles, and an output-destination code. The underlying QR command theme and the ability to use formulas or methods (not just fields) as cross-tab data sources are still present in current 4D and the generic-method pattern shown remains a sound, reusable design technique for report-heavy applications. As with the other 2003-era Quick Report notes, though, 4D Write Pro has since emerged as the more commonly used tool for building modern, flexible reports, so this specific QR-based generic method is a still-functional but now less frequently chosen approach for new report engineering.
related_updates: The QR command theme (QR SET REPORT KIND, QR SET INFO COLUMN, QR SET TOTALS DATA) and the ability to use formulas/methods as data sources remain part of current 4D and continue to work as shown

4D Write Pro has since become the more commonly used tool for building flexible, modern reports, though the classic Quick Report cross-tab engine and the generic-parameterized-method design pattern demonstrated here remain valid options
